summary: Feed s126_double to SIEM is degraded: 9.3% duplicate packets and 2.2% TCP packet drops detected. Other visibility checks (VLAN, one-way, truncation, tunnels, encryption, overload, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: 9.3% duplicates (265/2858, threshold 5%) indicates the packet broker is forwarding the same packet twice - typically aggregating both sides of a link or two SPAN/mirror sources without deduplication. Feed name 's126_double' suggests dual-feed aggregation without dedup enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes ingest, storage and license on duplicate events, inflates event counts, skews correlation/analytics and can cause false positives while obscuring true rates. SIEM does not need both directions or full payload, so duplicates provide no value.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication on the aggregation point for s126_double to suppress identical packets arriving within a short window before forwarding to the 1G SIEM port.

findings.root_cause: 2.2% of TCP packets (61/2798) show sequence gaps indicating packets lost in the visibility path - typically SPAN oversubscription, packet broker buffer exhaustion during microbursts, or congested broker-to-tool link.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM misses event/flow segments causing incomplete correlations, missed detections and gaps in forensic timeline. Even though SIEM tolerates one-way and truncated payload, missing packets still create blind spots for detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Add buffering and distribute load to prevent broker drops; dedup will also reduce load by ~9%. If source is SPAN, investigate SPAN drop counters and consider replace_span_with_tap for lossless capture.
